description: Madrid-Barajas has four parallel runway strips, each with its own L/R designator: 18L/36R and 18R/36L (the west/terminal-side pair, roughly north-south) and 14L/32R and 14R/32L (the east pair, running diagonally NW-SE). Headings are given as TRUE. The Spanish AIP (ENAIRE AD 2-LEMD) states magnetic variation at LEMD is 0 degrees (epoch 2020, annual change 8.1' East), i.e. true and magnetic north are effectively the same here -- unlike LSZH (true, confirmed materially different from magnetic) or EGCC (unresolved, ~1 degree gap). This makes the true-vs-magnetic question low-stakes for LEMD specifically, but it has NOT been independently confirmed against a current AIP chart that the wind-report frame (METAR, reported true per ICAO Annex 3 outside the US) and the runway-heading frame actually line up -- see docs/LEMD_RUNWAY_RESEARCH.md section 2 and docs/NEW_AIRPORT_QUESTIONS.md section 2.
source: Headings: PilotNav true headings (177/357 for 18L/36R; 140/320 for 14L/32R, via its older 15L/33R label). 18R/36L and 14R/32L assumed to match their parallel partner, unconfirmed. Thresholds: Sprinkle.com, 31-10-2026. Not checked against the Spanish AIP -- see research doc.
